text:
A: Hey! Lee, isn't it? Daniel. How you doing, mate?
B: All right. How long are these, three minutes?
A: Three minutes, yeah. Quick fire. Where are you calling from?
B: Wakefield.
A: Wakefield, nice. Is that a rugby league scarf I spotted?
B: Trinity, yeah.
A: Love it. I'm Spurs, unfortunately. Half a season ticket.
B: Unlucky.
A: Ha, honestly, that's the general response. What do you do?
B: Sales rep. Builders' merchants. You?
A: Solicitor, commercial property. Leases, acquisitions, that kind of thing. City firm. Bit of a sales job too, to be fair, half of it's keeping clients happy. Drinks, padel, remembering whose kid's at which school.
B: Padel?
A: Yeah, it's like tennis in a glass box. A client plays, so I took it up.
B: You took up a sport for a client.
A: Ha, when you put it like that. It's actually good fun, though.
B: Right. I just take mine a bacon butty. Same result.
A: That's probably cheaper, honestly. Do you play anything?
B: Five-a-side, Wednesday nights. If me mum'll sit with me lad.
A: No way, I'm Wednesday five-a-side too. Cage in Battersea, uni mates and a couple of lads from work. Gets a bit tasty sometimes.
B: Ours gets heated. I argue every decision, apparently. There's no ref, so someone has to.
A: Ha, we've got one of those. I'm normally the one calming everyone down.
B: Course you are.
A: What's that mean?
B: Nowt. You look like the one who calms everyone down. Bet you've got a spreadsheet for who's paid for the pitch.
A: Okay, that's actually true. Colour-coded. Is that bad?
B: Me manager'd love you. He's always on at me about pipeline updates. I'm good at the selling bit, I just don't write it down.
A: To be fair, the selling bit's the hard bit. Anyone can do a spreadsheet. Getting someone to sign, that's the skill.
B: Yeah, that's what I tell him. He says do both.
A: Mate, that's every manager. Do you enjoy it, though?
B: It's all right. Want a better car out of it eventually. Regional manager or summat. Or get poached.
A: That's the dream, isn't it. Get poached. I'm angling for partner, couple of years hopefully.
B: What's that get you?
A: Honestly? Money, mainly. And you get to tell people you're a partner.
B: At least you're honest about it.
A: Ha. What music you into, then? You strike me as an Arctic Monkeys man.
B: Yeah, Monkeys, Oasis, Kasabian. In the car.
A: Same! Monkeys at Finsbury Park, few years back, unbelievable. Did you
B: Sheffield's better. Home crowd.
